stem: A parent asks how fluids should usually be offered at home when ketosis is suspected or confirmed while following a sick-day plan. Which option is best?

options.text: Liquids containing water and electrolytes every 5-10 minutes
No oral fluids until all ketones have cleared
Only plain water once the child feels thirsty
Wait for hospital assessment before offering any fluids

explanation: Liquids containing water and electrolytes every 5-10 minutes are recommended to support frequent small-volume hydration during ketosis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diabetes Sick Day Management

optionExplanations.A: Correct because frequent small volumes of liquids containing water and electrolytes are the recommended home approach when ketosis is suspected or confirmed.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the guidance is to offer frequent small amounts, not a single large drink at long intervals.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because fluids should still be given; withholding all oral intake is not the recommended sick-day approach.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because plain water alone is not the specific recommendation; the plan calls for liquids containing water and electrolytes.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because home fluid management should start promptly rather than waiting for hospital assessment before offering any fluids.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
